title: SSH key fingerprint
summary: An SSH key fingerprint is a hash of the public key, typically SHA-256 (base64-encoded) or MD5 (hex, colon-separated). Displayed when connecting to a server for verification.

notes: SHA-256 fingerprint: 'SHA256:' + base64-encoded SHA-256 hash of the public key.
MD5 fingerprint: hex bytes separated by colons (legacy, less secure).
Fingerprints are used to verify server identity (avoid MITM).
OpenSSH 6.8+ uses SHA-256 by default; older versions use MD5.
